answer: In an agent economy selling velvet fabric designs, garden plans, and bridge inspections, each job ticket carries a buyer-issued nonce and a signed compute receipt from an execution provider. The provider enforces one work quota per billing principal, while the market adds reputation only for tickets accepted by unrelated buyers. Accounts using one principal share a quota and reputation cap even if they change names. A real newcomer can build a history through distinct clients, but a swarm of aliases cannot create extra verified capacity or fake sales.
